20 The total weight of a motorbike and rider is 1800 N. The motorbike travels in a straight line at
constant speed up a hill at an angle of 30 to the horizontal.
30
horizontal
The useful output power of the motorbike is 36 000 W. The total resistive force due to air
resistance and friction on the motorbike and rider is 2400 N.
What is the speed of the motorbike?
A
8.6 m s–1
B
11 m s–1
C
15 m s–1
D
24 m s–1

hints: Notice the bike moves at constant speed up a $30^{\circ}$ slope, so the engine must overcome both the $2400\text{ N}$ resistive force and the component of the $1800\text{ N}$ weight acting down the slope.
Recall that for motion along the slope, the weight component is $W\sin\theta$ and that constant speed means resultant force is zero, so driving force equals total opposing force.
Use useful power $P=Fv$ with $P=36000\text{ W}$ and $F=2400+1800\sin30^{\circ}$ to solve for $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: At constant speed the forces along the slope are balanced, so the forward driving force $F$ must equal all forces acting down the slope.
The downhill component of weight is $W\sin\theta = 1800\sin30^{\circ}$. Since $\sin30^{\circ}=0.5$, this is $1800 \times 0.5 = 900\text{ N}$.
Add the resistive force: $F = 2400\text{ N} + 900\text{ N} = 3300\text{ N}$ down the slope to be overcome.
Useful output power for a force parallel to velocity is $P=Fv$. Rearrange to $v=P/F$.
Substitute $P=36000\text{ W}$ and $F=3300\text{ N}$: $v = 36000/3300 \approx 10.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which is about $11\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with correct units. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses the full $1800\text{ N}$ weight added to $2400\text{ N}$, giving $36000/4200$. Only the component of weight down the $30^{\circ}$ slope opposes the motion.

B.explanation: Driving force balances $2400\text{ N}$ plus $1800\sin30^{\circ}=900\text{ N}$, so $v=36000/3300 \approx 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This is $36000/2400$, which ignores the work done against gravity when moving up the $30^{\circ}$ hill at constant speed.

D.explanation: This is $36000/(2400-900)$, which wrongly subtracts the downhill weight component instead of adding it to the resistive force.
